R17 completes historical issuance and governor/vote-source root review at Ethereum block 26124975; attester signing-policy evidence remains scoped unknown. The fallback stays unbounded-adverse, internal-ledger accounting supplies no reconciliation uplift, and no D29 certificate is authored.

review.evidence: R17 re-reviewed the current verified sources and authenticated the entire Ethereum block 26006832–26124975 history in one pinned eth_getLogs response: USDfr 198 events, MintRedeemController 51, FRGovernor 20, timelock 34, GROVE 7 and sGROVE 11. USDfr has 29 mint and six burn events; their net amount exactly equals pinned totalSupply 5142565558477829991308833 raw units. Historical mint/burn transaction inputs were reviewed alongside controller events, bootstrap role revocations and the FRV-007 token upgrade. No unexplained mint, burn, role grant or upgrade was identified. This is an issuance-control incident review, not independent reserve assurance. Issuer status, security disclosures, audit register, published governance and independent incident-index searches were also reviewed; disclosed open economic findings are fork scenarios, not live issuance incidents, and remain material risks. FRGovernor token() binds immutable GroveVotesAggregator 0x297ab97621b8b7734bbb0da6a4047ea873da5b04; its grove()/sGrove() bind the documented two sources. Verified FRGovernor authorizes upgrades onlyGovernance and disables pointer-only timelock replacement. GROVE and sGROVE remain mutable through timelock-held UPGRADER_ROLE; complete role histories and pinned membership retain that adverse vote-source authority, rather than treating aggregator immutability as immutable voting power. The timelock retains its 172800-second delay and the treasury has exercised decisive 1-billion-GROVE votes. No independent electorate, attester-human independence, D29 execution certificate or governed-issuance uplift is asserted. The established unrestricted minter-authorization economics, unbounded-adverse posture and internal-ledger reconciliation are unchanged. Earlier oracle-proxy binding, attester roster and treasury topology findings remain applicable; the separate scoped signing-policy question is retained.
